title: AI literacy in K-12: a systematic literature review
extended_summary:
This paper examines how artificial intelligence (AI) literacy is being introduced into K-12 education worldwide. The authors conduct a systematic literature review to map the landscape of AI education in schools, identify the main kinds of approaches being used, and highlight gaps in the evidence base. Their central question is how current approaches integrate AI literacy into K-12 education across different countries and settings.

The review is based on a Scopus search that ultimately included 179 documents. The authors classify the literature into two broad categories: learning experiences and theoretical perspectives. Learning experiences include activities aimed at helping students recognize AI in everyday artifacts, understand how AI works, use AI-related tools, and reflect on AI’s broader social and ethical implications. Theoretical perspectives include curriculum design, AI as a school subject, student perspectives, teacher training, support resources, and gender diversity. The review also notes country-level initiatives, especially in the United States, China, Singapore, Germany, and Canada, which are developing curriculum frameworks and implementation models for AI education.

The main conclusion is that K-12 AI literacy is still in an early stage and is often focused on technical or applied skills in limited domains, with very few studies rigorously assessing learning outcomes. The authors argue that AI literacy should be competency-based, interdisciplinary, integrated into existing subjects rather than added as a separate subject, and co-designed with teachers. They also emphasize the need for stronger attention to ethics, social consequences, and teacher preparation.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a peer-reviewed systematic literature review with transparent search and screening procedures, but it is not an experimental or quasi-experimental evaluation of an intervention. The evidence is therefore useful for mapping the field and identifying gaps, but it does not provide direct causal evidence.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper has important descriptive and agenda-setting relevance for K-12 AI education policy and curriculum design, but it reports no measurable intervention effect sizes. Its impact is mainly indirect: informing expectations and design choices rather than demonstrating student or institutional gains.

finding.finding_summary: This is a systematic literature review of 179 K-12 AI literacy papers, so it does not estimate a causal effect on student learning. It finds strong growth in AI literacy initiatives worldwide, with learning experiences and theoretical/policy proposals emerging, but also notes that most school-based experiences do not rigorously assess learning outcomes and that implementation is uneven across countries.
finding.measure: Systematic review of K-12 AI literacy literature; bibliometric and qualitative coding of 179 documents
